s: the seats next the orchestra, reserved for the Council
6906.full: 1. of or for the council or the councillors , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. able to advise or deliberate , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 3. as Substantive, βουλευτικόν, in the Athen. theatre, the seats next the orchestra, reserved for the Council , (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. the senatorial order , (Plutarch) (ML)

6912.full: βραβεύω (βραβεύς, an umpire), [in LXX: Wis.10:12 * ;] __(a) prop., to act as umpire; hence, __(b) generally, to arbitrate, decide (Isocr., Dem.; Lft., Col., l.with; MM, see word): Col.3:15; __(with) in some late writers, to direct, rule, control (so in Col., l.with, accusative to Thayer, see word, Meyer, in l.), (cf. κατα-βραβεύω). † (AS)

s: to cause to sink, to sink
6916.full: βυθίζω (βυθός), [in LXX: 2Ma.12:4 * ;] trans., to cause to sink, to sink: metaphorically, εἰς ὄλεθρον, 1Ti.6:9; pass., to sink, intrans.: Luk.5:7.† (AS)

6917.full: 1. a gulf, pit :—; at Athens a cleft behind the Acropolis, into which criminals were thrown, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. metaphorically ruin, perdition , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

6918.lxx: in LXX: Tob.13:17 (-ύλλιον in Exo.28:20, שֹׁהַם *
6918.full: βήρυλλος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ, [in LXX: Tob.13:17 (-ύλλιον in Exo.28:20, שֹׁהַם * ;]) beryl, a jewel of sea-green colour: Rev.21:20.† (AS)

6919.full: βίωσις, -εως, ἡ (βιόω), [in LXX: Si prol. 12 * ;] manner of life: Act.26:4.† (AS)

6921.full: 1. to stuff , 2. with genitive rei, to stuff full of , only in Pass., νήματος βεβυσμένος stuffed full of spun-work or yarn, (Odyssey by Homer); τὸ στόμα ἐβέβυστο [i.e. χρυσοῦ] (Herdotus Historicus) 3. with dative rei, to stop or bung up with, plug : Pass., σπογγίωι βεβυσμένος (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. absolute, βεβ. τὰ ὦτα deaf , (Lucian) (ML)

6940.full: γενέσια, -ων, τά, neut. pl. of adj. -ιος, -ον, relating to birth (γένεσις); __1. in Attic Gk., a commemoration of the dead. __2. In late Gk., a birthday feast (= cl. γενέθλια; so in π., see MM, Exp., x; cf. also Ῥutherford, NPhr., 184): Mat.14:6, Mrk.6:21. † (AS)

6941.full: γενεαλογέω, -ῶ (γενεά, λέγω), [in LXX: 1Ch.5:1 (יחשׁ)* ;] to trace ancestry, reckon genealogy; pass., before ἐκ: Heb.7:6.† (AS)

6948.full: 1. of or for geometry, geometrical , (Plato Philosophus): γεωμετρικὴ (i.e. τέχνη), geometry , (Plato Philosophus) 2. skilled in geometry, a geometrician , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

6950.full: γλεῦκος (-εος), -ους, τό, [in LXX for יַיִן, Job.32:19 * ;] must, sweet new wine (Arist.): Act.2:13.† (AS)

6952.full: flatter; to flatter with a tongue

6954.full: γναφεύς, -έως, ὁ, Ion. and κοινή form of Att. κναφεύς (κνάπτω, to card wool), [in LXX for כָּבַס, 4Ki.18:17, Isa.7:3 36:2 * ;] a fuller, cloth-dresser: Mrk.9:3.† (AS)

6965.full: γυμνάζω (γυμνός), [in LXX: 2Ma.10:15 * ;] __1. properly, to exercise naked. __2. Generally, to exercise, train the body or mind: 1Ti.4:7, Heb.5:14 12:11, 2Pe.2:14. † (AS)

6966.full: γυμνότης, -ητος, ἡ (γυμνός), [in LXX for עֵירֹם, Deu.28:48 * ;] nakedness: Rom.8:35, 2Co.11:27, Rev.3:18.† (AS)

6969.lxx: in LXX: 1Ch.4:8 (מִשְׁפָּחָה), Ecc.7:2 (ילד ni.; γένεσις, Aא), Wis.3:13 א 1 (γένεσις, ABא 2), Sir.22:3 *
6969.full: γέννησις, -εως, ἡ, [in LXX: 1Ch.4:8 (מִשְׁפָּחָה), Ecc.7:2 (ילד ni.; γένεσις, Aא), Wis.3:13 א 1 (γένεσις, ABא 2), Sir.22:3 * ;] __1. begetting. __2. birth: Mat.1:18, Luk.1:14, Rec. † (AS)

s: the ground between two lines of battle
6970.full: 1. a dyke, dam or mound to bar a stream, in plural, (Iliad by Homer); the phrase πολέμοιο γεφύραι seems to mean the ground between two lines of battle , = μεταίχμιον, (Iliad by Homer) 2. a bridge , to cross a stream, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; (Homer) also seems to recognise this sense in the Verb γεφυρόω. (ML)

6973.full: 1. like γονή, that which is begotten, offspring, a child , (Iliad by Homer); ὁ Πηλέως γ. his son , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. any product , of the silver mines at Laureion, (Aeschulus Tragicus); of tribute, (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. ἐς ἔρσενα γόνον to any of the male sex , (Herdotus Historicus) 4. like γένος, one's race, stock, descent , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

6989.full: 1. the power of a master over slaves, or the relation of master to slaves, (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. absolute sway, despotism , (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

6994.full: 1. to lead the people , in bad sense, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. with accusative pers. to win by popular arts , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)
